Laura — thanks for the clear asks. Please find attached our formal response to Section 3 and supporting artifacts. Short summary up front:

- Test harness & synthesis: We use a hybrid harness (k6 + Redwood runner) that supports both recorded (replayed customer traces) and synthetic traffic. All traces are sanitized using deterministic token redaction prior to lab ingestion. Lab runs are orchestrated in isolated namespaces; results are exported as CSV and plotted automatically.
- Baselines (representative): open-model-2k (2k context) steady-state p50/p90/p99: 85ms / 220ms / 430ms at 100 QPS/GPU. open-model-8k (8k context): 170ms / 410ms / 980ms at 40 QPS/GPU. Detailed CSVs are attached.
- Warmup & cold-start: We define warm workers as those with KV cache > 80% populated. Warmup protocol: 10-minute prefix warm with varied prompts; cold-start penalty is ~2.5x on initial requests and decays back to baseline within ~30 seconds of sustained traffic. Repro instructions included.
- Degradation & fallback: automatic routing to quantized model variants, dynamic per-replica concurrency throttling, and cross-region failover when available. We publish the exact fallback decision tree in the runbook.
- Repro artifacts: bench_plan_lab_instructions_v1.pdf, load_profile_samples.csv, p99_plots.png, sla_evidence_snapshots.zip.
